D1:
Core is the lowest AnimationPriority (Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2-4). The default Animate script plays idle/walk at Idle/Movement priority, so on any joint both animate, the higher priority wins and your swing loses on the arms. Fix: make it Action (re-export with priority Action in the Animation Editor, or set it in code). Also load the track once through the Animator, not Humanoid:LoadAnimation (deprecated) on every click, which keeps creating tracks.

local char = player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()
local animator = char:WaitForChild('Humanoid'):WaitForChild('Animator')
local track = animator:LoadAnimation(script.SwingAnim)
track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action
tool.Activated:Connect(function()
    if not track.IsPlaying then track:Play(0.05) end
end)

Reload the track on CharacterAdded after respawn.
D2:
1) Server: each client has its own Workspace.CurrentCamera, and the client controls it. A server Script setting workspace.CurrentCamera only changes the server's camera object, which is not replicated to anyone, so nothing happens. 2) Client: CameraType is still Custom, so the default PlayerModule camera scripts rewrite Camera.CFrame every frame (RenderStep) and your one-off assignment is overwritten on the next frame. Fix in a LocalScript: wait for the camera, set CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable, then set/tween the CFrame; when the cutscene ends set CameraType back to Custom (and CameraSubject to the Humanoid).

local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
cam.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable
cam.CFrame = workspace:WaitForChild('CutsceneCam').CFrame
-- ... later
cam.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Custom
D3: CanvasSize is a fixed 600 px; it does not grow with the content, so with 40 items the list extends past the canvas and the extra rows are unreachable (with few items there is empty scroll space). Cleanest fix: set ScrollingFrame.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y and CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0) (scale must be 0 on the auto axis, else it adds on top). Alternative/legacy: listen to UIListLayout:GetPropertyChangedSignal('AbsoluteContentSize') and set CanvasSize = UDim2.fromOffset(0, layout.AbsoluteContentSize.Y + padding). Also avoid scale-based Y sizes on children (they scale with the canvas); use offset heights or UIAspectRatioConstraint, and include UIPadding in the calculation.
D4: 1) Too little force: weight = AssemblyMass * workspace.Gravity. A 20x2x20 plastic part is 800 studs^3 * 0.7 = 560 mass units; with gravity 196.2 that needs ~110,000 force just to hover, so 5000 does nothing. 2) Force is applied at a corner attachment, so it also creates torque and tips the part. 3) RelativeTo defaults to Attachment0, so the force is in the attachment's local frame; once tilted the 'up' vector points sideways and pushes the platform away, which tilts it more (runaway sliding/spinning). Correct setup: put the attachment at the center of mass (or set ApplyAtCenterOfMass = true), set RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World, Force = Vector3.new(0, part.AssemblyMass * workspace.Gravity, 0) (recompute if mass changes; add a small extra or a PD term to rise/hold height). Add an AlignOrientation (or AngularVelocity/damping) to keep it level, and for height-holding prefer AlignPosition or a controller rather than a raw constant force.

local function attachPet(pet: BasePart, player: Player)
  local hrp = (player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()):WaitForChild('HumanoidRootPart')
  pet.Anchored = false; pet.CanCollide = false; pet.Massless = true
  local a0 = Instance.new('Attachment'); a0.Parent = pet
  local a1 = Instance.new('Attachment'); a1.Name = 'PetSlot'
  a1.Position = Vector3.new(0, 2, 3) -- +Z is behind (LookVector is -Z)
  a1.Parent = hrp
  local ap = Instance.new('AlignPosition')
  ap.Attachment0 = a0; ap.Attachment1 = a1
  ap.MaxForce = 1e6; ap.Responsiveness = 20; ap.Parent = pet
  local ao = Instance.new('AlignOrientation')
  ao.Attachment0 = a0; ao.Attachment1 = a1
  ao.MaxTorque = 1e6; ao.Responsiveness = 20; ao.Parent = pet
  pet.Parent = workspace
  pet:SetNetworkOwner(player)
end

Rules: pet must be unanchored and not welded to the character; Massless + CanCollide false so it doesn't push/affect the player; two-attachment mode means no per-frame code (target moves with HRP); attachment Position offsets are in HRP local space (behind = +Z); tune Responsiveness/MaxForce instead of RigidityEnabled for smoothness; set network owner to the owning player (same owner as the HRP) to avoid stutter; parent movers before/with the part; clean up on CharacterRemoving.

local PathfindingService = game:GetService('PathfindingService')
local function walkTo(humanoid: Humanoid, target: Vector3)
  local root = humanoid.Parent.HumanoidRootPart
  local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({
    AgentRadius = 2, AgentHeight = 5, AgentCanJump = true,
    Costs = { Lava = math.huge, Water = 20 },
  })
  local ok = pcall(path.ComputeAsync, path, root.Position, target)
  if not ok or path.Status ~= Enum.PathStatus.Success then return false end
  for _, wp in path:GetWaypoints() do
    if wp.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then humanoid.Jump = true end
    humanoid:MoveTo(wp.Position)
    if not humanoid.MoveToFinished:Wait() then return false end
  end
  return true
end

Rules: Costs keys match PathfindingModifier.Label and terrain Material names (Water); math.huge = never traverse, a finite high cost = avoid unless no reasonable route; modifier volumes need PassThrough = false (and CanCollide false parts are fine); AgentCanJump enables Jump waypoints, which you must act on by setting Humanoid.Jump; wrap ComputeAsync in pcall and check Status (NoPath); MoveTo times out after 8s, so wait per waypoint; listen to path.Blocked to recompute; SetNetworkOwner(nil) on the NPC root for consistent server movement.

-- (a) music, client LocalScript (or server for everyone), not spatial
local function wire(src, dst)
  local w = Instance.new('Wire'); w.SourceInstance = src; w.TargetInstance = dst; w.Parent = dst; return w
end
local music = Instance.new('AudioPlayer')
music.Asset = 'rbxassetid://MUSIC_ID'; music.Looping = true; music.Volume = 0.5
music.Parent = game:GetService('SoundService')
local out = Instance.new('AudioDeviceOutput'); out.Parent = music

music:Play()

-- (b) spatial campfire
local fire = workspace.Campfire
local crackle = Instance.new('AudioPlayer')
crackle.Asset = 'rbxassetid://CRACKLE_ID'; crackle.Looping = true; crackle.Parent = fire
local emitter = Instance.new('AudioEmitter'); emitter.Parent = fire
emitter:SetDistanceAttenuation({[0] = 1, [10] = 0.6, [40] = 0})

local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local SUB_ID = 'EXP-1234567890'

local function refresh(player: Player)
  local ok, status = pcall(MarketplaceService.GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync, MarketplaceService, player, SUB_ID)
  local active = ok and status.IsSubscribed or false

D11: Cars: give the driver network ownership of the whole vehicle assembly while seated (VehicleSeat does this by default for the occupant; or explicitly call chassis:SetNetworkOwner(occupantPlayer) on Occupant change and SetNetworkOwner(nil) or auto when they leave). Driver-side physics removes input latency, so driving feels responsive. Implication: the owning client has full authority over that assembly's physics, so an exploiter can teleport/fly the car or ram things with it. Mitigate with server sanity checks (max speed, position deltas, teleport distance, being inside allowed areas), revoke ownership/reset on violations, don't let car position drive important logic (finishes, kills) without validation. NPC guards: call SetNetworkOwner(nil) on all their parts (root) so the server simulates them, otherwise automatic ownership hands them to the nearest player, letting exploiters fling/freeze/teleport them and causing desync. Even with server ownership, exploiters can still push them with parts they own (e.g. their car/character), so cap velocities, use collision groups between player-owned vehicles and NPCs if needed, and keep AI/damage logic server-side. General: ownership is only physics authority; never trust client-owned positions for hits, loot, or rewards.
D12: Standard DataStores are versioned automatically: each write creates a version (snapshotted roughly at most once per hour per key, so several writes inside an hour can collapse into one), and versions are kept for 30 days (the latest version is kept indefinitely). APIs: DataStore:ListVersionsAsync(key, Enum.SortDirection.Descending, minDate, maxDate, pageSize) returns DataStoreKeyPages of DataStoreObjectVersionInfo (Version, CreatedTime, IsDeleted); DataStore:GetVersionAsync(key, version) reads that snapshot; DataStore:GetVersionAtTimeAsync(key, timestampMs) directly returns the version active at a timestamp (ideal: pass the update's release time). Restore by writing that value back as the current value with SetAsync/UpdateAsync (keep the userIds and metadata from DataStoreKeyInfo). Tool design: admin-only command or Open Cloud endpoint (Open Cloud DataStore API also lists/gets versions) taking UserId + timestamp; preview the old data, then write it; the player must be offline or kicked first and the session lock released, otherwise their live server overwrites the restore on save; log every restore. Limits: 30-day window; hourly granularity, so a version just before the update may include data from up to an hour earlier or be merged; restore loses progress made after the update; requests count against DataStore budgets; doesn't apply to OrderedDataStores; deleted keys are recoverable only within the window.
D13: (1) Announcements: the panel backend calls the Open Cloud MessagingService API (POST .../universes/{universeId}/topics/{topic}:publish, API key with messaging-service:publish scope). Every server does MessagingService:SubscribeAsync('Announcements', ...) and shows the message (validate/size-limit text, max 1 KB, best-effort delivery). (2) Item grants: write the grant durably first, then notify. Backend writes to the player's 'pending grants' (Open Cloud DataStore entry like Grants_<userId>, or a MemoryStore queue/sorted map for short-lived) with a unique grantId. Then it publishes a MessagingService message 'grant' with the userId. The server that has the player online consumes it: UpdateAsync on the pending key to atomically remove the grant, add the item to the player's session data and save. Offline players: on join, the server checks the pending key and applies it. Don't let the panel write directly into the live player-data key, because the online server's session would overwrite it. Use idempotency (track applied grantIds) so retries/duplicate messages don't double-grant. Security: API keys stored server-side only, least-privilege scopes limited to this universe, IP allowlist and expiry, panel auth + audit log; Roblox servers treat messages as commands only from the trusted topic and validate payloads.
D14: BindableEvent/BindableFunction arguments are serialized and copied across the call, like remotes: tables are deep-copied, metatables are stripped, functions are dropped, mixed/non-string keys can be lost, and Instances pass by reference. So the receiver gets a plain data table without the class metatable, so methods like inv:AddItem() are nil, and changes made to the copy don't affect the original object (two diverging states). Also identity checks fail (copy ~= original). ModuleScripts fix this: require() returns the same cached table to every Script in the same environment (server vs client), so you share real objects and call functions directly with no serialization. Typical design: one or a few Scripts as entry points, the rest as service modules (InventoryService, CombatService) that expose functions like InventoryService.get(player) returning the live OOP object; modules communicate through direct calls or a custom signal module (pure Luau signal that passes values by reference). Benefits: type checking/autocomplete, explicit dependencies, no timing races of BindableEvents firing before listeners connect. Keep Bindables only where you need decoupled cross-environment or Instance-based events, and pass ids/data instead of objects there.
D15: UnreliableRemoteEvent is meant for high-frequency, ephemeral, cosmetic data where only the latest value matters: aim direction, look angles, footstep/VFX triggers. Messages are unordered and may be dropped (no resend), and they don't queue behind or block reliable traffic, so the reliable RemoteEvents (hits, purchases) are no longer delayed by them. Constraints: payload is small (about 1000 bytes per call; larger sends are dropped), so send compact data (e.g. a quantized Vector3 or buffer), never anything that must arrive or arrive in order (damage, purchases, state changes, start/stop pairs: use a reliable event or make each packet self-contained state); OnServerEvent/OnClientEvent API is the same; still validate and rate-limit on the server (exploiters can spam it), and type check. Also reduce load: lower the rate (10-20 Hz) and interpolate on receivers, send only on change, broadcast only to nearby players, and don't re-broadcast footsteps that other clients can derive from replicated animation/position.
D16: Problems: (1) Message size limit is 1 KB, so a 3 KB payload fails. (2) Publish limit per server is about 150 + 60 x players per minute, and more importantly per-topic delivery limits: each topic can receive roughly 10 + 20 x number of servers messages per minute, and a single subscriber is capped too; 500 servers x 12/min = 6000 publishes/min all fanning out to 500 subscribers (3 million deliveries/min), so it gets throttled and messages are dropped. (3) Delivery is best-effort: no guaranteed delivery, no ordering, no persistence, so a server that subscribes late or misses a message has a stale/incomplete list, and dead servers never 'unpublish' (need TTLs). (4) Each server must hold and parse the whole list (memory/CPU), and subscriptions per server are limited. Better: store each server's entry in a MemoryStore SortedMap/HashMap keyed by JobId with a short expiration (e.g. 30s), refreshed every ~15-30s with a small payload (counts, not full player lists); lobby servers read with GetRangeAsync paginated when the browser is opened. Use MessagingService only for small, rare events (e.g. join requests).
D17: Limits: HttpService allows 500 requests per minute per server (all external HTTP shares it; Open Cloud calls from inside count too), requests can fail/timeout, and HttpEnabled must be on. Per-request external APIs also have their own rate limits (429). Calling 3x per join + per kill on busy servers hits these spikes. Correct setup: batch/queue analytics events server-side and flush every N seconds or when the batch is full (one request carrying many events), with pcall, exponential backoff and a bounded queue; drop non-critical events when over budget; consider built-in AnalyticsService (custom/economy/funnel events) instead of an external API. Secrets: never hard-code the API key in a script (anyone with place access, Team Create collaborator, leaked place file or model can read it). Store it in the experience's Secrets store (Creator Hub > Secrets, scoped to allowed domains) and read it with HttpService:GetSecret('name'), which returns a Secret object you can only use in headers/URLs via HttpService requests (AddPrefix/AddSuffix). Give the Open Cloud key minimal scopes, restrict to this universe, set expiry, and rotate the leaked key now.
D18: Camera (client): update in RunService:BindToRenderStep('CamFollow', Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, fn) (or RenderStepped / PreRender). Heartbeat runs after physics, not tied to the render step; setting the camera there means it uses positions from a different point in the frame than what is rendered, and it conflicts with the default camera scripts that run at Camera priority, so you get jitter. Using the render step with the camera priority runs right before the frame is drawn, using current character positions, so it's smooth. Server projectile: RenderStepped/BindToRenderStep/PreRender exist only on clients (no rendering on the server), hence the error. Use RunService.Heartbeat (PostSimulation) or Stepped/PreSimulation, and move by dt each step (pos += vel * dt), ideally with raycasts between previous and new positions; or use a shared fixed simulation step. Rule: client visuals/camera = render step; server or physics logic = Heartbeat/PreSimulation/PostSimulation.
D19: For a new 2026 cross-platform game use the Input Action System (IAS); ContextActionService still works but IAS is now the recommended, data-driven approach and is what Roblox builds new controls on. Structure: InputContext instances (groups of actions, enabled/disabled and with Priority/Sink to layer contexts, e.g. Gameplay vs Menu) contain InputAction instances (Type Bool/Direction1D/Direction2D/ViewportPosition etc., e.g. 'Sprint', 'Interact'), and each action contains InputBinding children mapping physical inputs (KeyCode such as LeftShift/E, gamepad ButtonL3/ButtonX, a touch UI button via the UIButton property, composite Up/Down/Left/Right for directions). Scripts listen to InputAction.Pressed/Released/StateChanged or GetState(), so game logic is device-agnostic and users/devs can rebind by editing bindings. Contexts can live in StarterGui/ReplicatedStorage and be cloned to the player. Default player scripts: Roblox is replacing the legacy PlayerModule (ControlModule/CameraModule Lua scripts forked into StarterPlayerScripts) with new default movement/camera controls built on IAS, so movement can be customized by editing input actions/bindings instead of forking the PlayerModule; legacy forked scripts are being phased out, so avoid forking them in a new project.
D20: Server Authority is an opt-in mode (in beta in 2025, rolling out in 2026) enabled per place through Workspace's authority setting (Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server) in Studio. It makes the server authoritative over physics and character movement: clients no longer own their characters/assemblies in the traditional sense; the client predicts locally from its inputs and the server simulates the real state, then rolls back and resimulates the client when they disagree. Result: speed/teleport/fly/fling exploits via network ownership stop working, and hits are evaluated on consistent state, while movement stays responsive. What changes in scripts: gameplay that affects simulation must be driven by input that is sent to the server, not by client-set positions or velocity (use the Input Action System for inputs); custom movement/abilities must run as deterministic simulation code in the fixed-step simulation callback (RunService:BindToSimulation) on both client and server so it can be predicted and replayed; avoid client-only physics changes, reliance on SetNetworkOwner tricks, and wall-clock/frame-rate-dependent logic; state that matters for rollback should be registered/replicated as predicted state (attributes etc.) rather than mutated arbitrarily; test with network simulation. Purely visual client code (VFX, UI, camera) is unchanged.
D21: Use RunService:BindToSimulation(callback) (the fixed-timestep simulation API introduced with Server Authority in 2025/2026). It runs your movement code at a fixed simulation rate (60 Hz) with a constant dt, independent of the render frame rate, and on both client and server in lockstep, so results match and can be predicted and resimulated (rollback). PreSimulation fires once per frame with a variable dt, so 30 vs 144 FPS integrate differently and the server's tick differs. Requirements: enable Server Authority on the place (Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server); code inside the callback must be deterministic, using only the provided dt and inputs read through the Input Action System, not os.clock, math.random without a shared seed, render-only values or client-only state; it may be called multiple times for resimulation, so it must not have side effects like firing remotes, spawning VFX or yielding; apply movement via physics/character state, not by setting CFrame from the render loop; keep the code in both client and server reachable locations (e.g. a shared ModuleScript).
D22: Lighting.Technology was deprecated (2025). It is no longer shown in the Properties window and is not scriptable at runtime: it was never meant to be changed by a LocalScript, and now writing it errors. It was replaced by two new Lighting properties: LightingStyle (Realistic vs Soft look) and PrioritizeLightingQuality (a bool letting the engine use the highest quality lighting the device supports, where Future-like quality is used automatically and scales down on weak devices). The engine now picks the actual technology per device based on these plus the user's graphics quality. Settings menu fix: don't try to switch technology; remove the code. Offer quality options via things you can change, e.g. toggling post effects (Bloom, SunRays, DepthOfField), shadows on lights/parts, Atmosphere, particle counts, or render distance, and set LightingStyle/PrioritizeLightingQuality in Studio (they are also designed as place-level, not per-player runtime toggles).

D24: All but remap-from-scratch have new builtins, and remap has one too: lerp -> math.lerp(a, b, t) (added 2025, exact at t=1). remap -> math.map(x, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax) (already in the math library; no need to hand-roll). NaN check -> math.isnan(x) (added 2025 together with math.isinf and math.isfinite).
